page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test, Geekbench single-core score of 2855.0, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 5146.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, fall into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth remains average, measuring 47.98 GB/sec for large-block read operations.

The server exhibits performance limitations under parallelized workloads, as evidenced by poor prompt processing speeds on medium-sized language models and weak static web serving throughput. However, its high memory density and strong single-thread execution make it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallelization. Appropriate workloads include database operations, text processing, and lightweight single-threaded caching or compression tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. Single-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core results ranking in the top tier. However, multi-threaded performance and parallel processing capabilities, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium LLM inference, are average to weak. This resource profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound, single-threaded workloads, database operations, and text processing tasks, while representing a performance tradeoff for highly parallelized or compute-heavy applications.
